title: Spike: agent doc create/update — validate the MCP write surface that already ships at HEAD, and find the real gap
description:
## Problem (premise corrected — read this first)
The team's working assumption is that AFFiNE offers no feasible way for an agent to create or update a page, leaving socket.io collaborative sync as the only write path. **That was true, and is now out of date.** Upstream shipped server-side document write tools over MCP in PR toeverything/AFFiNE#14245, 'feat(server): add document write tools for mcp', commit 0da91e406e (2026-01-16). That commit introduced BOTH core/doc/writer.ts and the MCP write tools, and it is already in this fork's tree — it arrived with the v0.27.4 merge (eac15e21bd) and is present at woven/main 0761a62ba1.

The deferral the team remembers is real and correctly recalled, just superseded. Maintainer darkskygit on toeverything/AFFiNE#13500 (closed 2025-11-15): AFFiNE has 'basic mcp support, it allow you read and search document', and 'write support is still under development and will be gradually opened in future versions'. #14245 is that opening, landing ~2 months later.

So this is very likely an ENABLEMENT and VALIDATION problem, not a build-an-editing-API problem. Scope this spike to proving that — or disproving it — before anyone designs a fork-local API.

## What already exists at HEAD (verified 2026-08-29 by reading the tree)
  Endpoint:  POST /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/mcp   (plugins/copilot/mcp/controller.ts)
             marked @Public(), authenticated by bearer token via McpCredentialService
             (credential.ts: list / create / rotate / revoke, scoped per workspace+user)
  Tools:     read_document, doc_search, create_document, update_document, update_document_meta
             (plugins/copilot/mcp/provider.ts)
  Write gate: the three write tools are registered only when accessMode === McpAccessMode.READ_WRITE
             (a Prisma enum; default in provider.for() is READ_ONLY)
  Mechanism: DocWriter.updateDoc(workspaceId, docId, markdown, editorId) reads the current doc binary,
             calls the native Rust updateDocWithMarkdown (packages/backend/native/src/doc.rs:370 ->
             doc_loader::update_doc, y-octo), which STRUCTURALLY DIFFS and returns ONLY A DELTA,
             then storage.pushDocUpdates([delta]) and emitDocUpdatesPushed to broadcast to live clients.

That last point matters: this is not a clobbering whole-doc overwrite. It produces a real CRDT delta and broadcasts it, so a concurrent human editor converges by normal Yjs merge rather than losing work. The shape is right.

## The residual risks worth actually testing (this is the spike's value)
1. **Markdown is a lossy projection of a BlockSuite doc.** update_document takes markdown as the COMPLETE new content and block-diffs against it. Anything markdown cannot express is a data-loss candidate: edgeless/canvas layout and positioning, embeds, database/table blocks, comments, custom doc properties, attachments. A round-trip (read_document -> unchanged markdown -> update_document) SHOULD be a no-op; if it silently drops blocks, that is the real gap and it is a serious one.
2. **Read-modify-write with no visible CAS.** writer.ts does getDoc(...) then pushDocUpdates(...) with no lock or compare-and-swap between them; core/doc/storage/lock.ts exists but writer.ts does not use it. Yjs merge covers a lot, but the DIFF is computed against a base that may already be stale, so a concurrent edit could produce a delta that reverts a block. Test this deliberately with a simultaneous editor.
3. **update_document does not touch the title** — its own docstring says so; title goes through update_document_meta. An agent that 'updates a page' via one call will silently leave a stale title.

## Enablement gates to confirm
  - The MCP controller is registered inside the COPILOT plugin module (plugins/copilot/index.ts:82 lists WorkspaceMcpController), so reaching it requires the copilot plugin enabled. Whether that in turn demands a configured AI provider is the key unknown — if it does, this work depends on affine-p2d (configurable AI/LLM endpoints), which is already on the roadmap.
  - No AFFINE_PRO / license gate was found around the MCP or copilot code paths, but confirm rather than assume.
  - Find how McpAccessMode.READ_WRITE is actually set for a credential (resolver.ts / GraphQL surface), since READ_ONLY is the default.

## Pointers (discovery queries)
  - Grep: 'WorkspaceMcpProvider', 'McpAccessMode', 'McpCredentialService', 'updateDocWithMarkdown', 'pushDocUpdates'
  - Rust: packages/backend/native/src/doc.rs -> update_doc_with_markdown / update_doc_title
  - Upstream history: 'git show 0da91e406e --stat'; issues toeverything/AFFiNE#13500 and #13262
  - Third-party reference doing this the hard way (WebSocket/Yjs sync, create/edit/delete): github.com/DAWNCR0W/affine-mcp-server — useful as a comparison, NOT as a dependency
  - Authored against commit: 0761a62ba1

## Why now
Cheap and high-information. If the surface works, a key team workflow unblocks for roughly the cost of configuration, and epics affine-rqo (Claude Desktop), affine-m07 (agentic API) and affine-def (Slack) all inherit a working write path instead of each inventing one. If it is lossy, we learn that BEFORE designing a fork-local API, and the loss cases become the actual spec.

## Scope discipline
This is a time-boxed SPIKE per affine-3os: investigate, produce a design note, propose decomposition. Do NOT build a fork-local editing API here — the whole point is to establish whether one is needed. Note also that SHIPPING write access to agents is gated on affine-1a4 (security / external-surface threat model); this spike's investigation is not, but any rollout is.

## Model tier
design-spike
acceptance_criteria:
1. Round-trip fidelity measured, not assumed: on a doc containing at least one edgeless/canvas element, one database or table block, one embed, and custom doc properties, call read_document then feed the UNCHANGED markdown to update_document. Record precisely which blocks and properties survive and which are dropped. A clean no-op and a lossy result are both acceptable OUTCOMES; an untested guess is not.
2. Concurrency behaviour observed under a real race: begin an update_document call while a browser client holds the same doc open with unsaved local edits, and record whether the human's edit survives, is reverted, or merges. State whether the missing compare-and-swap in writer.ts is a practical problem or only a theoretical one.
3. Enablement path written down as literal steps that a second person can follow on the woven self-host: which config enables the copilot plugin, whether a configured AI provider is required (and therefore whether this depends on affine-p2d), how an MCP credential is issued, and how McpAccessMode.READ_WRITE is set. Include the exact curl for POST /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/mcp with a bearer token that successfully creates a document.
4. A written verdict answering the question this spike exists for: is the fork's remaining gap (a) configuration only, (b) configuration plus a bounded set of loss cases worth patching, or (c) large enough to justify a fork-local editing API. Name the evidence behind the verdict.
5. Follow-on beads filed with bd dep add --type discovered-from, sized to one deployable PR each. Do not leave the outcome as prose only.

title: CI guard: fail when an upstream-owned file is edited without a scripts/woven-patch-manifest.md row
description:
## Problem
scripts/woven-patch-manifest.md is the fork's tracked list of deliberate divergence from upstream, and it is CURRENTLY UNENFORCED. It is a markdown document that nothing reads. affine-hn1's own framing is 'the CI guard's job is to fail when an upstream-owned file is modified WITHOUT a row here' (manifest, line ~14) and affine-cm9 requires 'CI must block them from upstream-directed branches/PRs'. Neither exists.

Verified 2026-08-29 @ 0761a62ba1: the only fork-owned workflow is .github/workflows/woven-publish-image.yml (a build/push job); the sole reference to the manifest anywhere under .github/ or scripts/ is prose in scripts/woven-agent-bootstrap.md.

## Why now
The manifest just proved it cannot police itself. affine-hn1.1 shipped a manifest that OMITTED packages/backend/server/src/seed/index.ts even though that same commit's divergence audit had already named it — the manifest was in violation of its own rule from the moment it was written, and it took a human re-reading to catch. That is exactly the failure a guard makes impossible. Cost of a miss compounds: an unmanifested fork patch is silently reverted by the next 'clean' upstream merge, and nobody learns until production breaks (which is how this fork got here — see the x-affine-client-kind CORS incident in affine-hn1.1).

## Context
Cheap to build because the inputs already exist and are exact:
  - upstream-owned vs fork-owned is decidable: 'git diff --name-only <merge-base> HEAD'; fork-owned files are the ones ABSENT at the merge base. At v0.27.4 this yields 26 changed / 3 upstream-owned, so the guard has a known-good fixture to test against.
  - the manifest table is a pipe-delimited markdown table with the path in backticks in column 1 — parseable without a markdown library.

## Pointers (discovery queries, not file:line — paths rot)
  - Grep: 'Diverged upstream-owned files', 'FORK-LOCAL CORE PATCH', 'ADDITIVE' in scripts/woven-patch-manifest.md
  - Existing fork CI to model style/shape on: .github/workflows/woven-publish-image.yml, scripts/woven-ci-min.sh
  - Merge-base derivation: the manifest's own 'Merge-time checklist' step 1 (merge from a stable upstream tag)
  - NOTE the trigger trap documented in the manifest checklist step 6: build-test.yml's push: list covers canary/beta/stable/v*.x, NOT woven/*. A guard wired only to push: will never run on this fork. Wire it to pull_request: (and workflow_dispatch:) or it is decorative.

## Model tier
well-specified-impl
acceptance_criteria:
1. A guard script (scripts/woven-manifest-guard.sh or equivalent) exits NONZERO when run against a tree where an upstream-owned file is modified with no manifest row, and exits ZERO on woven/main @ 0761a62ba1 (the known-good fixture: 3 upstream-owned files, 3 rows).
2. Regression fixture proves the affine-hn1.1 miss is now caught: with the seed/index.ts row deleted from the manifest, the guard exits nonzero and names packages/backend/server/src/seed/index.ts in its output.
3. The guard runs in CI on pull_request: targeting woven/main (NOT only push:, which does not fire for woven/* — see manifest checklist step 6). Demonstrated by a run URL where the job actually executed.
4. Guard output names every offending path, so the fix is mechanical rather than a re-audit.
5. Every row in the manifest resolves to a path that exists in the tree (catches rows left behind after upstream deletes a file).

title: bug: woven-build-image.sh never applies scripts/woven.dockerignore (temp-name BuildKit ignores) -> root .dockerignore silently used; woven.dockerignore also excludes tests/ which breaks yarn --immutable
description: scripts/woven-build-image.sh copies scripts/woven.dockerignore to .dockerignore.woven.$$ at repo root, but BuildKit only reads <context>/.dockerignore or <dockerfile>.dockerignore, so that temp file is never used — the local from-source build has actually been governed by the committed root .dockerignore all along (which correctly keeps tests/blocksuite/packages/tools workspaces). Separately, scripts/woven.dockerignore excludes tests/ and **/dist,**/lib; using it as the real context ignore drops the 8 tests/* workspace package.json and makes 'yarn install --immutable' fail with YN0028 (lockfile would be modified) — hit live in CI run 29293390322 for affine-3ab.1. Fix options: (a) delete the dead temp-file logic + stale scripts/woven.dockerignore and rely on root .dockerignore, or (b) rename woven.dockerignore to scripts/woven.Dockerfile.dockerignore AND remove its tests/ exclusion. Discovered during affine-3ab.1 GHCR publish spike.

title: Import multiple .bs.zip snapshots at once
description:
Allow importing several .bs.zip snapshot files in one action (currently single-file only).

## Where it lives (recon, commit 5b7f83a6e)
- Import dialog: packages/frontend/core/src/desktop/dialogs/import/index.tsx -- the 'snapshot' entry in importConfigs sets fileOptions.multiple:false and its importFunction throws unless exactly one file ('Expected a single zip file'). handleImport already threads a File[] through, so the plumbing supports multiple.
- Transformer: ZipTransformer.importDocs(collection, schema, blob) in blocksuite/affine/widgets/linked-doc/src/transformers/zip.ts accepts a SINGLE Blob (no loop).
- Picker: openFilesWith(acceptType, multiple) in blocksuite/affine/shared/src/utils/file/filesys.ts already supports multiple (default true); the 'Zip' accept type matches .zip so .bs.zip is accepted.

## Fix (small: config + loop)
1. Set snapshot fileOptions.multiple:true in import/index.tsx.
2. Rewrite the snapshot importFunction to iterate files and call ZipTransformer.importDocs per file, concatenating docIds (optionally add a Blob[] overload in zip.ts for shared asset-SHA dedup).
Additive frontend change -- upstreamable (good-neighbor candidate; NOT a fork-local patch).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] The snapshot import picker allows selecting multiple .bs.zip files
- [ ] Importing N files creates docs from all N (docIds length == N), verified in an affine-local e2e
- [ ] Single-file import still works unchanged
- [ ] Asset collisions across zips do not corrupt blobs (dedup by SHA)
